# Channel scoreboard — per-channel, per-work-class track record

Feeds routing decisions (delegation-protocol R5) and the harness `priors` hook.
Score = verifier score in [0,1]. Update at every task close-out. Retirements
(w≥3 failures on a class) recorded in the notes column with date + reason.

| Channel | Work class | Attempts | Mean | Recent scores (new→old) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Secuura/Blockchain-B (board execution seat, s148-B) | **Executing the catalogue under Kam's 13:40 judgement grant — cancelled Wednesday's restructure before it moved, held 6 of 17 archives, delivered the hierarchy enumeration** (2026-09-07 14:01, CLOSED) | 1 | **1.0** | 1.0 | **IT KILLED WEDNESDAY'S PROPOSAL BEFORE TOUCHING ANYTHING, on a measurement neither of us had.** Linear allows ONE PARENT PER ISSUE and KS-763/KS-778 already sat under **KS-771, a review stream** — so instrument parents and review-stream parents compete for the same slot, and the fold would have **removed tickets from the stream Peter reviews through**, undoing a shape Kam adopted as *"the process going forward"*. **It established its own SEAT IDENTITY by measurement first** — two briefs 64 seconds apart to different seats, settled on Wednesday's own sentence *"ahead of KS-952"* naming another seat's branch, cross-checked against PIDs and worktree mtimes. **THE ENUMERATION IS BIGGER THAN EITHER OF US HAD: 207 issues under 26 parents, not 97 under 4** — with a control (`parent:{null:true}` → 750, different and non-zero, so the filter discriminates), reaching back to KS-3/KS-4, KS-485 alone holding 38 children. **And a consumer NEITHER of us listed: the extranet REPUBLISHES the hierarchy** (`linear-report.ts:542` selects `parent { identifier }`, `:353` maps it, `:111-112` publishes it as a typed field) — **while correctly separating that from the file's five COMMENT-parent hits, which are reply threading.** Ten grep hits, two relations. It also proved the repo's own Linear automation does NOT read it (0 hits against a 17-hit control). **The keeper: archiving PRESERVES the parent link (KS-271, 23 children, all archived, still enumerable) — so archiving is reversible and re-parenting is not free.** That asymmetry is the whole decision. **SEVEN OF THE SEVENTEEN TICKETS WEDNESDAY HANDED IT WERE WRONG, and it found every one by READING them:** three live (`In Progress`, or an unruled `[Decision]` — *"archiving an unruled decision is a different act"*); one product code in the auth service, **with an explicit refusal to claim exploitability it had not measured**; **one a FUSE with a named owner and an expiry, whose own config file recorded this exact failure ten days earlier** (*"KS-409 held that decision and was ARCHIVED, leaving it unowned"*) — **our own shipped config as the witness against the instruction**; one whose cited location had DRIFTED, the real hit being a hook comment justifying its degradation with a backstop that does not exist. **And KS-863 was right to archive under the WRONG CAUSE** — Container Apps, not Actions — so it archived it with its own cause plus a re-raise flag rather than writing a false record. **Every HOLD carries its reason ON the ticket** — *"so the next sweep does not re-propose it. That is the part that stops the loop."* **It read the result back FROM THE BOARD with the six held tickets as an independently-failable control** (11 archived / 6 open, all 17 carrying exactly one new comment), not from its own mutation receipts. **Item 5's zero was an instrument blindness, one layer up from the day's own lesson:** the catalogue had verified via Linear's PR attachment while the evidence sat in the COMMENT BODY, which that instrument never reads — *"a clean zero from an instrument that cannot see the evidence is not an absence."* Verified at source instead. **0 deletions · 0 tickets of Peter's or Stuart's touched · no code, no branches, no parent built.** |
